causalModel.founding: Founded at the Panther fork on springs that can be drunk unboiled.
causalModel.siteAdvantages: Firm ground where clean water rises at a stone lip, at the last dry footing before the Helstrom approach.
causalModel.occupantsMotive: The tribe is the interior's last friendly stop. It charges nothing for water and a great deal for beds and rope.
causalModel.pressures: The Hist is sick and the village blames salt from upstream. Helstrom traffic brings people the tribe would rather not host.
causalModel.wouldChangeIf: If the spring soured, the village would move within a season.

districts.notes: One common with the Hist, the spring and the landing.

why.what: A Hist village of seven buildings round an open common, with the spring house and the landing on the bank.
why.whyHere: Clean water rises here at the last dry ground before Helstrom.
why.whyNeighbours: It is the last friendly stop on the track to Helstrom; the refuge footpath runs along its bank.
why.playerPurpose: Beds and rope, free water, a trader and the shrine; the quests of the spring and the sick root start here.
why.microGeography: A slope falling west to the channel; the huts sit on mud pads and the Hist on a mound.

parcels.orientationWhy: Its door turns west to the common and the way down to the spring.

playerPurpose.note: Beds rented to travellers on the Helstrom road, at a high price.

why.what: The lodge, where the bed-keeper rents beds and sells rope.
why.whyHere: The village lives by being the last friendly stop before Helstrom; it charges for beds, not water.
why.whySpot: The first dry shelf a traveller reaches from the track, on the east side of the common.
why.whyNeighbours: It faces the common across from the Hist shrine; the root-herald's house stands to the north.
why.playerPurpose: A bed for the night in a safe room; rope for the road.
why.microGeography: A mud pad cut into the slope, graded down to the common.

parcels.orientationWhy: Its door turns south onto the common.

playerPurpose.note: The root-herald buys from travellers and sells what comes down from Helstrom.
The herald keeps the upriver salt the village blames for the sick root.

why.what: The root-herald's house, where the village trades with Helstrom.
why.whyHere: The root-herald carries the village's trade to Helstrom and back.
why.whySpot: The north edge of the common, on the widest flat ground.
why.whyNeighbours: It looks across the common to the lodge and the Hist.
why.playerPurpose: A trader who keeps the salt that starts the argument over the sick root.
why.microGeography: A mud pad on the north shelf, above the wet ground by the water.

parcels.orientationWhy: Its door turns north-west to the Hist and the shrine.

playerPurpose.note: The tree-minder can say what ails the Hist.

why.what: The tree-minder's house beside the Hist.
why.whyHere: A Hist village keeps its tree-minder close to the tree.
why.whySpot: On the rise east of the Hist, the nearest dry pad to its roots.
why.whyNeighbours: The Hist and its shrine are across the path to the west; the lodge is to the north.
why.playerPurpose: The person who speaks for the Hist and can start MR01.
why.microGeography: A mud pad cut into the side of the Hist's rise.

parcels.orientationWhy: Its door turns north to the spring house.

playerPurpose.note: The spring-keeper knows who uses the water and when it turned.

why.what: The spring-keeper's house, above the spring.
why.whyHere: The spring-keeper and her family live beside the water they keep.
why.whySpot: South of the spring house, on the last dry ground before the bank.
why.whyNeighbours: The spring house is below it to the north; the Hist stands up the slope to the east.
why.playerPurpose: A home to enter and a witness for LH38.
why.microGeography: A mud pad on the low slope above the channel bank.

parcels.orientationWhy: Its door turns south-east to the common.

playerPurpose.note: Talk of the delegations that camped elsewhere (LH51).
A family that cooks for travellers and hears their talk.

why.what: A family hut on the west side of the common.
why.whyHere: The families of the village live round the common.
why.whySpot: West of the herald's house, where the ground runs down to the water.
why.whyNeighbours: It faces the common with the herald's house to the east.
why.playerPurpose: A home to enter, where the family talks of the delegations that camped elsewhere.
why.microGeography: A mud pad on the gentle slope above the bank.

parcels.orientationWhy: Its door turns west toward the common and the herald's path.

playerPurpose.note: A family that sits out and watches who comes down the track.

why.what: A family hut on the north-east edge, by the track.
why.whyHere: The village has grown up the slope toward the track.
why.whySpot: North of the lodge on a dry shelf beside the track.
why.whyNeighbours: It looks down the path to the common and the herald's house.
why.playerPurpose: A family who can say who came down the track and when.
why.microGeography: A mud pad cut into the upper slope above the lodge.

parcels.orientationWhy: Its open front turns east to the path from the common.

why.what: The spring house, a roofed shelter over the stone lip where the water rises.
why.whyHere: The village was founded on water that can be drunk unboiled.
why.whySpot: On the bank where the spring rises, beside the footpath along the water.
why.whyNeighbours: The spring-keeper's house is just south; the landing is north along the bank.
why.playerPurpose: Clean water poured free; LH37 and LH38 both turn on this spring.
why.microGeography: Low ground above the channel bank, on a mud pad.

parcels.orientationWhy: The totems face the common, in front of the Hist.

why.what: The shrine at the foot of the Hist: totems, candles and flowers.
why.whyHere: Every Argonian place keeps a shrine at its tree, not a temple.
why.whySpot: On the flat ground round the Hist's roots, facing the common.
why.whyNeighbours: The Hist is behind it; the tree-minder's house is across the path to the east.
why.playerPurpose: The shrine service and the start of MR01 at the sick root.
why.microGeography: The Hist's mound, levelled round its roots.

routes.why: The way from the track's end down through the common to the footpath on the bank.
From the common to the lodge door.
From the common to the root-herald's door.
From the way to the family hut.
From the herald's path to the east family hut.
From the way to the tree-minder's door.
From the way to the spring house.
From the spring house up to the spring-keeper's door.
From the bank footpath down to the boats.
From the common to the shrine at the Hist.

landmarks.notes: The village's tribal Hist, ailing (MR01); hist-placement R2 tribal, R3 state sick.

why.what: The village's Hist, a broad old tree whose roots are sickening.
why.whyHere: Most Argonian tribes build round their Hist; this village was founded at the spring and its tree.
why.whySpot: On the mound above the common, where the slope levels before it falls to the water.
why.whyNeighbours: The shrine is at its foot and the tree-minder's house beside it.
why.playerPurpose: The landmark seen from the track; its sick root is the subject of MR01.
why.microGeography: A raised mound of mud round its roots, on the slope above the channel.

occupants.cultureRole: the root-herald who trades with Helstrom

approaches.sequence: Coming down the track from the Border road, the Hist crown shows first over the trees, then the lodge roof and the smoke from the common.
approaches.wayfinding: The track ends at the top of the village; the way runs down past the tree-minder's house to the common.

approaches.sequence: Walking up the footpath from the south-west, the spring house and the jars at its lip show first, then the Hist above it and the canoes on the bank beyond.
approaches.wayfinding: The footpath passes the spring house; the way up to the common leaves it just past the spring.

networkTerminals.why: The track from the Border road comes down the ridge and turns into the village at its east corner.
The footpath from the refuge comes up the channel bank and enters at the spring house.

combatSpaces.why: The open common between the huts, where a fight in the village happens.

scaleGrounding.loreSource: settlement-register row Greenspring (M3, a freshwater village at the fork); record npcs merchant (single) and family (band); notable slots tree-minder, root-herald, spring-keeper
scaleGrounding.why: Five households and the lodge's guests. Seven buildings stand: six houses and the spring house, round one common with the Hist and the landing.

candidates.why: The west-facing slope between the track's end and the channel bank: dry ground above the water, the refuge footpath along the bank.
The plotted anchor, at the end of the track from the Border road.
candidates.rejectedBecause: Slopes of 6 to 10 degrees and 90 m from the water; no room for a landing or the spring.
